analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is a wind O&M services company trading at 81x earnings and 22x sales despite near-zero profitability (ROE 1.02%) and seven years of revenue stagnation — a valuation completely divorced from fundamentals. At ₹6,549 Cr market cap, it is 6-65x outside my SMILE sweet spot and offers no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Debt dramatically reduced: borrowings collapsed from ₹1,411 Cr (2021) to ₹95 Cr (2025), D/E now 0.05
Promoter holding 56.12% — skin in the game, above my 50% threshold
India's wind energy expansion provides a structural tailwind for O&M services long-term
key_risks: Valuation is grotesque: EV/EBITDA 129x and P/S 22x for a services business with ₹236 Cr revenue — any disappointment causes massive drawdown
Revenue has gone nowhere in 7 years (₹368 Cr in 2018 → ₹236 Cr in 2025, CAGR -6.1%); no growth story to justify premium
Profitability is razor-thin: net profit ₹22 Cr on ₹6,549 Cr market cap — one bad wind season erases earnings entirely
red_flags: Market cap ₹6,549 Cr is 6-65x outside my SMILE sweet spot — institutional investors have already discovered and priced this
P/E 81.6x vs my max threshold of 15x for small-caps — paying 5x too much even assuming perfect execution
Other income surged from negative to +₹57 Cr in FY25, masking weak core operating performance (operating income contracted to ₹52 Cr)
Subsidiary of Inox Wind — lacks independent decision-making, strategic agenda set by parent
Free cash flow negative in 3 of last 5 years; FY25 investing CF -₹637 Cr funded entirely by equity dilution (financing CF +₹572 Cr)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my SMILE lens, Inox Green fails on virtually every parameter. It is not small (₹6,549 Cr), it is not cheap (P/E 81x, EV/EBITDA 129x), and it has not demonstrated the revenue velocity I need — top-line was ₹368 Cr in 2018 and is only ₹236 Cr in 2025. The company did just turn profitable in FY24-25, but at ₹22-28 Cr net profit against a ₹6,549 Cr market cap, the market is pricing in decades of flawless execution. ROE of 1.02% and ROCE of 2.60% are not the signatures of a business with pricing power or competitive moat.

The one genuinely positive story here is the balance sheet transformation — borrowings fell from ₹1,411 Cr to ₹95 Cr, and the company raised fresh equity in FY25 (financing CF +₹572 Cr), likely to fund the ₹637 Cr investing outflow (possibly wind farm acquisitions or power generation expansion). If that capital deployment generates meaningful revenue and profitability, the story changes. But at current valuations I am paying for that future today, with zero margin of safety. I need to see revenue cross ₹500-600 Cr, margins expand, and ROE above 15% before this conversation is worth having — and even then, not at ₹6,549 Cr market cap.
